ledger.claim: This dispute rests on a single, internally consistent trip, so the rider's case is properly founded: EV-TRIP-00804, EV-GPS-00804 and EV-FARE-00804 all carry trip_id TRP-00804, and the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown agree on the 13:54 booking, the 13:59:30 arrival and the 4.88 km driven. The same-trip condition in POL-RD-08(a) is met and the burden of explanation passes to the driver under POL-RD-08.

The trace the rider's case rests on is clean and carries its full weight: EV-GPS-00804 holds 79 fixes over 100% coverage on a 10-second sample interval, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 10 seconds, so it is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) and nothing in this case turns on an impaired artifact; the case can be decided on the trace itself without any escalation under POL-RD-10(3), and the artifact stands at weight 1.0 under POL-GEN-02.

On the POL-RD-01 threshold test the governing measurement is the GPS polyline, not the rounded convenience copy: EV-GPS-00804 records trace_distance_km of 4.88 km between the recorded pickup event and the recorded dropoff event, and that is the figure the excess must be run on.

I have to concede the threshold is not met, and I will not stretch the point. Measured against the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km, the trace shows an excess of 0.13 km, which is 2.74% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be BOTH greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and neither test passes, so no route deviation is established on this trip and the rider's refund claim fails on the evidence as measured.

The claim as filed also measures the trip against the wrong baseline, and I concede that ground too: the rider's 3.10 km figure is solo_optimal_distance_km, but TRP-00804 is a RYDE_POOL trip and under POL-RD-12 the baseline for POL-RD-01 is the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km, with the solo estimate carried for reference only. Distance attributable to collecting the co-rider at Queenstown is never a deviation, so no part of it is refundable to the rider.

For completeness on the driver's side of the ledger: no traffic advisory covers this trip at all. EV-ADVIS-00804-01 is MISSING, carries issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and a weight_multiplier of 0.0, so under POL-GEN-02 it can carry no fact. I disclose that impairment expressly. If any external traffic cause is later advanced, POL-RD-13 gives such an assertion no weight where no advisory covers the trip window and POL-RD-03 is unavailable on this record — though I note no such cause is in fact asserted on the present record.

The rider's claim is measured against the wrong baseline. This trip is RYDE_POOL, so under POL-RD-12 the POL-RD-01 baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km recorded on the trip record at booking, and not the solo-rider estimate of 3.10 km the rider cites. POL-RD-12 states in terms that a claim which measures excess against solo_optimal_distance_km has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone. The record is complete on this point and no POL-RD-10(5) gap arises: the trip record identifies the pooled itinerary through vehicle_type RYDE_POOL and optimal_route_source PLATFORM_MATCHED_ITINERARY_AT_BOOKING, and carries the matched itinerary as optimal_distance_km.

On the correct pooled baseline the trace shows no deviation at all. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, 4.88 km, against the matched-itinerary optimal of 4.75 km — an excess of 0.13 km, or 2.74%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal and 0.8 km in absolute terms; this excess fails both limbs by a wide margin, and the policy's own derived deviation block records the status as 'no deviation'. Where the trace figure and the trip record's rounded copy agree, as they do here, nothing turns on the choice, but the trace is the field that governs.

The very thing the rider complains of — the collection of another passenger at Queenstown — is excluded from excess by POL-RD-12. The trip record's own event log confirms the matched pooled itinerary at 13:55 and states that the co-rider pickup at Queenstown is included in the 4.75 km estimate. Distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary is never a deviation. The rider's central factual allegation, even if true, is therefore not a route deviation in law.

Even if a deviation were established, POL-RD-02 would refund nothing. Recomputed on the booked optimal route — (3.80 + 0.75 x 4.75 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee — the fare is 12.0825 SGD, which EXCEEDS the 11.90 SGD actually charged. Refund = charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero, so the refund is 0.00, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and the outcome is NO_ACTION in any event. The ledger's own derived money block computes refund_before_rounding of 0 and marks the refund below de minimis.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The trace is COMPLETE and is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a) to (c): 79 fixes at a 10 second sampling interval, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 10 seconds. There is therefore no impaired-trace route to an independent corroborating source under POL-RD-07(ii), and the ordinary POL-RD-01 threshold test applied to that clean trace fails. An assertion of excess that cites no evidence id of its own carries no weight.

No billing-integrity correction is available to the rider under POL-RD-09(4). The fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines and no tolls (both 0.00) and no airport surcharge; the 0.80 SGD platform fee is a standard structured line of the fare model. There is no charge line that the trace or the trip record fails to match, so the one route to a refund that is available whether or not a deviation exists is closed.

Even if the materiality gate had been reached, POL-RD-06 discloses no pattern against this driver: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 300 completed trips in the same window — below the 3-flag trigger and a ratio of 0.00, far under the 0.05 threshold. There is no basis for the balance to be resolved against the driver, for a FULL_REFUND uplift, or for a conduct referral, and no other profile field is used for that test.

Every artifact the driver relies on carries weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes fired, so no disclosure obligation arises and no discount attaches to the finding under POL-GEN-02. The only impaired artifact in the bundle is the traffic advisory, which the driver does not rely on and does not need, because no deviation was established that would require exoneration.

NO_ACTION is the correct outcome and on this record it is a win for the driver. The rider filed this dispute, payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so leaving the present state standing preserves the fare the driver earned on a completed pooled trip. The driver asks that the claim be dismissed; he does not ask for the fare to be varied, and no compensation is sought because the billed distance of 4.88 km equals the trace distance, leaving no unbilled shortfall above 1.0 km.

ruling.explanation:
The fare you were charged stands, and the refund you asked for is not due. The reason is the baseline the claim uses. Trip TRP-00804 is a RYDE_POOL trip, so under POL-RD-12 the figure the route-deviation test runs against is the platform-matched pooled itinerary of 4.75 km stored on EV-TRIP-00804, not the solo-rider estimate of 3.10 km in your claim. The solo figure is carried on the record for reference only, and the clause says a claim measured against it cites the wrong field; the driver's and your own advocate's briefs both correct this. Measured the right way, EV-GPS-00804 records a trace of 4.88 km over a clean export (79 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps), giving an excess of 0.13 km, or 2.74% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and neither limb is met, so no route deviation is established on this trip. The distance used to collect the co-rider at Queenstown is separately excluded from excess by POL-RD-12, so the collection itself is not a deviation in law however inconvenient it was. The arithmetic confirms the point from the other direction: on EV-FARE-00804 the charged_total is SGD 11.90 and the recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 4.75 + 0.28 x 14.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 12.0825, so the refund under POL-RD-02 is charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero — SGD 0.00, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis. No billing-integrity correction is available under POL-RD-09(4): the fare breakdown carries no ERP gantry lines, no tolls and no airport surcharge, and the SGD 0.80 platform fee is a standard line of the fare model, so there is no unmatched charge to refund. There is no repeat-deviation pattern under POL-RD-06 — the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 300 completed trips in the same window, well under both triggers — so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral arises. The only impaired artifact in the bundle is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00804-01 (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0); it can carry no fact, and because nobody asserts an external traffic cause for this trip, its absence decides nothing and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. No driver compensation is due either: the billed distance of 4.88 km equals the trace distance, so there is no unbilled shortfall. The route-deviation claim is therefore dismissed on the evidence: under POL-GEN-03 the present state stands, the charge remains in place and nothing is refunded. Confidence is 0.95, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-GPS-00804, EV-TRIP-00804, EV-FARE-00804) that carry the deciding measurements; the monetary effect is nil, below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold. This ruling is provisional, and either party may appeal it once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
